newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac asked to track Nazi in Syria.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac asked to track Nazi in Syria.

text.p: The Simon Wiesenthal centre called on French President Jacques Chirac on Friday to bring up with Syrian authorities this weekend the case of Alois Brunner, the most notorious Nazi war criminal still at large.

Chirac is expected in Damascus on Saturday on the first leg of a Middle East tour and the Paris office of the Nazi-hunting body said in a statement it hoped he would renew a French demand for Brunner's extradition during their talks.
Brunner was World War Two deputy to fellow Austrian Adolf Eichmann, the man to whom Nazi leader Adolf Hitler entrusted the extermination of six million Jews.
Both French and German authorities have said in the past they believed he was hiding in Syria.

"The latest news of Brunner still points to his presence in Damascus under the alias Georg Fischer. Your visit is an appropriate occasion to relaunch the suspended French demand for Brunner's extradition," the centre said.
Brunner is alleged to have ordered the deportation of Jews from Austria, Greece, Czechoslovakia and France, where he was once head of the notorious Drancy transit camp.
The Wiesenthal centre says Brunner is responsible for 143,000 deaths, including thousands of French citizens.
